pagerduty-bot: [AUTOPAGE] service=inference-gateway env=prod-usw2 metric=5xx_rate value=5.8% threshold=3.0% — oncall: oncall-sre. Pager: fired. Incident link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345
Sam Liu: acked in PD — I'm on it. Anyone touching recent canaries? :eyes:
Tara Ng: I hit a quick snooze (2m) to quiet the noise while we looked — the bot re-fired shortly after. Did the threshold re-evaluate too aggressively? :thinking:
incident-bot: Snooze applied by Tara Ng for 2m. Autopage resumed because 5xx persisted above threshold for >1m. Top failing path: POST /v1/generate -> upstream 502/504 clustered on auth-proxy pool
Devon Park: checking dashboards — grafana shows a tight spike starting at 1809991120. CPU/memory on pods fine. Error traces show lots of `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `context deadline exceeded` from auth-proxy -> model-sidecar.
Sam Liu: good call. Any recent deploys to auth-proxy or model routing?
Devon Park: canary rollout for routing rule `weight:v2=10%` deployed ~10m ago (canary id c-20260315-7). Suspect the new routing increases persistent connections and exposed a keepalive bug.
Henry Kim: I'm watching logs. A handful of nodes show repeated `read tcp ... connection reset by peer` from the keepalive handshake. Looks like TCP keepalive window too short on the mesh sidecar.
Tara Ng: suggestion: rollback canary to v1 immediately and re-route traffic to stable until root cause fixed. Also avoid snoozing autopage until we confirm mitigation.
Tilly Ramos: routing change: shifting canary back to 0% now (console). Confirming via API...
Tilly Ramos: done — `POST /api/routing/rollout` returned 200. moving 100% -> v1.
Devon Park: running `kubectl rollout undo` on auth-proxy deployment as quick mitigation. Command I'm using:
```
kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/auth-proxy --to-revision=42
```
Sam Liu: thanks. After rollback, can everyone watch 5xx rate in the next 5 minutes? I'll keep PD acked but monitoring.
pagerduty-bot: [UPDATE] Escalation: page escalated to support-lead because initial snooze overlapped with sustained error window.
Henry Kim: after rollback, 5xx rate dropped from 5.8% -> 0.9% in ~3m. Latency also returned to baseline. Looks like rollback mitigated it.
Sam Liu: excellent. Devon — can you open a PR to fix keepalive defaults + add stricter connection metrics? Add a regression test for persistent connection churn.
Devon Park: will do. Drafting PR and linking to this thread. Plan: bump keepalive idle to 120s, timeout to 30s, add circuit-breaker to abort on N consecutive resets. Target merge + canary tomorrow morning.
Tara Ng: action item: update runbook to warn against early snooze of autopage for sustained signals. We need a short PD runbook line: "Confirm customer impact before snooze; verify spike shape (brief vs sustained)"
Sam Liu: agreed. Severity: Sev2 (partial degradation, customer-visible errors for ~12 minutes). Impact: ~3% of requests affected at peak for prod-usw2; no major customers reported data loss.
Tilly Ramos: monitoring alert policy: I'll add a secondary check that requires >1m sustained over threshold to reduce noisy re-fires during short blips.
incident-bot: Incident closed by Sam Liu — mitigation: rollback canary and adjust routing. Follow-ups: PR for keepalive config (Devon), runbook edit (Tara), PD suppression policy tweak (Tilly).
Sam Liu: closing thread here. Good job team — we'll run a short postmortem tomorrow and link actions. :thumbsup:
